chunks: Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd narrated to me from Salamah, from Ya’qūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Bakr ibn Muḥammad, from Fuďayl ibn Yasār, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
The sins of whoever cries, even as little as (the width of) the wing of a fly, when we are mentioned in front of him will be forgiven, even if his sins are greater than the scum in the sea.
Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh narrated to me from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ‘Abdillāh Al-Barqi, from his father, from Bakr ibn Muḥammad, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), similarly.

key_terms.ذُكِرْنَا: we are mentioned (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for crying when the Ahl al-Bayt are mentioned?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that even a single tear shed in remembrance of the Ahl al-Bayt, no matter how small, expiates sins as numerous as the sea's foam. This hadith, recorded in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, underscores the Shia theological view that emotional connection to the Imams serves as a potent mechanism for spiritual purification and divine mercy. The dual narration chains highlight the reliability and centrality of this practice in devotional life.
